justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Dysphagia management evidence base exists; BCS-S vs non-certified comparison not available.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: ASHA BCS-S portfolio plus exam; significant documentation requirements.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to SLPs specializing in dysphagia and swallowing disorders.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No BCS-S billing premium; standard SLP dysphagia billing applies.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate demand in acute care, inpatient rehab, and SNF SLP positions with dysphagia focus.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Patients with dysphagia value specialized SLP expertise.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Dysphagia care is almost entirely insurance/Medicare-funded; little cash-pay market.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: BCS-S can support modest consultative rates, but no consumer premium.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Held by only a few hundred SLPs nationally — genuinely rare credential, professionally.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Highly individual credential with strict maintenance; cannot scale across staff easily.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Direct-to-consumer demand is near zero; recognized only by hospitals and referral sources.
justifications.business.efficiency: Requires 350+ clinical hours in swallowing plus extensive portfolio and exam — slow and costly for business purposes.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Top-tier SLP specialty credential; explicitly valued for CSD faculty promotion and dysphagia course leads.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: BCS-S holders are typically active researchers and presenters in dysphagia science.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly maps to dysphagia content, a cornerstone of MS-SLP curricula.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Dysphagia field has strong and growing evidence base (MBSImP, IDDSI, instrumental assessment).
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Frequently preferred in dysphagia-focused SLP faculty postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Hours, portfolio, and exam requirements are demanding, lowering efficiency despite high payoff.
